sun.upright:
Look at the figure on the right-hand side of the wheel, the one with the jackal's head. He's on his way up, and he isn't climbing. The wheel is carrying him. For an Aries Sun that's a slightly awkward picture, because you like to get somewhere under your own steam and you like people to know you did. Cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, you'd rather earn the lift by force.

Jupiter is the Wheel's planet, the planet of luck and more of everything, and it has no special standing in Aries. It comes in as a visitor and picks up the manners of the house, and the house belongs to Mars, so whatever good fortune turns up has your temperament on it, quick and hot and wanting to move. There's real help in the chart as well. Sagittarius, Jupiter's own sign, is fire too and sits in an easy trine to yours, so when an opening appears you're usually first to see it and first through. The trouble is the gap before it appears. You can feel something good on its way, a job, a yes, some money, and the waiting drives you up the wall, so you try to hurry it and sometimes spoil it.

At work that tends to be the promotion that's genuinely coming and the email you want to send pushing for it a month early. With money it's the punt you fancy mostly because doing nothing feels like losing. A partner can get the same treatment, pressed for an answer before they've found one. Pick the opportunity you care about most and leave it alone for a fortnight.
sun.reversed:
With the Wheel upside down, an Aries Sun tends to grab the thing and try to spin it by hand. The timing's off, a plan keeps slipping, and Mars, which rules your sign, takes every delay personally. So you push. You force the deal through a week before it's ready, demand the answer, throw money at a chance because sitting still feels like falling behind, and a good run gets used up early. Reversed Jupiter can also make you overconfident about your own luck, which is its own kind of trouble.

It shows at work, in the project that falls over because it launched half-built, and with money, in the impulsive bet made out of restlessness. It can show with friends too, when you've been picking fights and can't quite say why. Notice the moment you want to force something, then leave it for a day and go and do something physical.

moon.upright:
Feelings come in quickly for an Aries Moon, and they leave quickly too, usually once you've done something about them. The Wheel adds Jupiter to that, and Jupiter makes things bigger. The good moods are very good, loud and warm and generous, and the bad ones arrive with the same force. Jupiter has no dignity in Aries, so it runs on Mars's terms here, which means fast.

The easy part is that you bounce. Sagittarius, the fire sign Jupiter rules, sits trine to Aries, and in practice that means optimism comes back to you almost by reflex. Most Aries Moons I've seen are over a disappointment by the next morning. The hard part is the bit in between, the flat afternoon when nothing's happening and you can't stand it. That's when you do something drastic just to feel a change. You quit the thing, send the message, book the flight, when another day would have shifted the mood on its own.

A partner will probably see it first, as the argument you start because an argument felt better than the flatness. Your body shows it late at night, wired, looking for somewhere to put the energy. And there's usually a friend who hears about a big plan on Monday that's gone cold by Friday. When the next low comes, go for a hard walk before you decide anything.
moon.reversed:
Stuck at the bottom of a mood, an Aries Moon with the Wheel reversed can't believe it will ever lift. Jupiter overdoes the low as easily as the high, so one bad day starts to look like proof that everything's gone against you, and Mars wants to fight its way out immediately. That's when the sudden change tends to happen, the resignation, the break-up text, the big purchase, and quite often that change is the mistake.

The people you live with get the snapped answers and the plans cancelled in a temper. Sleep goes, the mind still running laps at midnight. What helps is small and physical and has an end to it. Find a ten-minute job you can do with your hands, the dishes, a flat bike tyre, and finish it. Your mood will usually have moved a little by the time you're done, and you won't have anything to undo.

rising.upright:
Strangers usually meet an Aries Ascendant mid-stride. Mars rules your chart, and you come across as quick, direct, a bit of a challenge, already halfway into something. The Wheel on that entrance makes you look lucky as well, the sort of person who turns up just as a chance opens and gets it. Sagittarius, Jupiter's home sign, is trine to Aries, fire to fire, so the luck isn't fighting your speed. It rides along with it.

People are likely to read you as a chancer in the good sense, someone worth backing because you move while others are still thinking. What pulls the other way is timing. The Wheel turns when it turns, and an Aries Ascendant would sooner kick the door in than wait the extra beat for it to swing. From the inside, waiting feels like losing your nerve. From the outside, it can look like you barged through an opening that was about to be handed to you.

In a job interview it's the strong entrance that wins the room, and the risk of talking over the offer you came for. Meeting new people, you might propose the plan before they've sat down, which some will love and some will find a lot. In a negotiation you can move so fast that a better version of the deal goes past. When the next opening comes your way, count to three before you answer it.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, the Wheel can make an Aries Ascendant misjudge the moment. You come in fast expecting the door to swing open the way it usually does, and this time the timing's wrong, so the push reads as pushy. Jupiter's shine turns into overconfidence, the promise that's too big for a first meeting, the bet on your own luck that doesn't come off. Or it goes the other way, and you brace for bad luck and start things half-heartedly so you won't be caught out.

New colleagues hear the big claims and quietly knock a third off. A first date hears the confident talk and wonders what's underneath. Keep the nerve, it's the best thing about you. The habit to drop is reading one closed door as a judgement on your luck. Try one opening at a time, and promise only what you can deliver by Friday.

sun.upright:
There's a bull in the bottom corner of this card, sitting with an open book in front of it while the wheel turns overhead. It doesn't look bothered. A Taurus Sun could take something from that, because a card about everything changing is an odd thing to be handed when you've spent years making your life solid. Fixed earth, ruled by Venus, you build yourself on what lasts, and here's Jupiter saying good things move.

Jupiter has no special dignity in Taurus, so it takes its tone from Venus, and that softens it a lot. The luck on offer comes through pleasure and value and people who like you, through the slow, patient things you're already good at, and almost never through a wild bet. Pisces, one of the two signs Jupiter rules, is sextile to yours, a friendly angle that still has to be used, and it tends to bring fortune in sideways, a favour, an introduction over dinner. What gets in the way is that you can mistake holding a good thing tightly for keeping it safe. A lucky stretch held too hard doesn't grow into the next one. It just sits there, and you get tense guarding it.

With money, there's probably a chance to grow what you've built that you keep putting off because the current arrangement feels safe. At work it might be a role you've enjoyed that has quietly run its course. Your body can be part of it too, a routine that's stopped doing you any good and that you keep anyway. Say yes to the change that scares you slightly, and let one solid thing move.
sun.reversed:
The Wheel reversed can catch a Taurus Sun holding on and calling it good sense. Something's trying to change, a job, a house, an old arrangement, and you've decided that keeping it exactly as it is counts as stability. Mostly it's you refusing to budge, and it's tiring. Jupiter upside down can also run the other way, into too much, spending or eating or buying your way toward the good feeling the change would have brought anyway.

At work it's the role you've outgrown and won't leave because leaving feels like risk. With money it's either sitting on savings out of fear or a comfort splurge to get through a flat month. Find the thing you're gripping hardest and loosen one finger. You don't have to let go of all of it. Let one part change, and notice that the ground is still there.

moon.upright:
What settles a Taurus Moon is knowing things will stay put. The same bed, the same walk, the same person across the table. So a card whose whole message is that everything turns can land like a threat, even when it's bringing something good. Jupiter has no special standing in your sign and borrows Venus's manner here, so the way it moves your feelings is slow and warm. Contentment comes in big soft swells when life's going well, and when it dips you don't quite believe it'll come back.

Fixed earth holds a mood for a long time. When you're comfortable you want to freeze the day, and Jupiter keeps quietly pointing out that even a good feeling is a phase, which a Taurus Moon hears almost as a loss. The help comes from Pisces, which Jupiter rules, sitting sextile to Taurus. It gives you a softer way through, a way of noticing a change coming without bracing your whole body against it. Most Taurus Moons I've known feel better once they stop guarding the calm and simply have it.

A partner is often where it shows, when you're so content you start worrying it'll end and the worry spoils the evening. Food is another place, eating to hold a mood in place or to pad a low one. At home it's the routine you defend after it's stopped soothing you. When the next good stretch comes, enjoy it with the door open and don't count the days.
moon.reversed:
When the Wheel falls the wrong way for a Taurus Moon, a passing low gets treated as the new normal. Jupiter makes the dip bigger, fixed earth digs in, and you batten down with the usual comforts while you wait for a lift you've half decided isn't coming. The comforts overdo themselves. The extra helping, the third episode, the small purchase that fixes the mood for an hour.

A partner feels you go quiet and can't get a straight answer about what's wrong. Sleep gets longer without getting any better, and your body carries the stuckness as a heaviness in the arms and legs. Change one small thing on purpose, a different walk, a room rearranged, a new route to work, and see whether your feelings move with it. They usually shift a bit within a day or two.

rising.upright:
People meeting a Taurus Ascendant tend to relax. You look unhurried and comfortable, Venus rules your chart, and there's a sense that you've landed well wherever you are. With the Wheel drawn on that front, you look lucky as well, steady and a bit blessed, the person others assume has it sorted. Jupiter holds no rank in Taurus and works through Venus here, and Pisces, Jupiter's water sign, is sextile to Taurus, so openings tend to drift toward you through people who simply like your company.

Where the card and the sign disagree is timing. The Wheel wants you to move when the chance is there, and fixed earth likes to be certain before it shifts its weight. Jupiter keeps opening doors and you keep saying you'll think about it, and you do think about it, carefully, for a fortnight, while the door slowly closes. It feels like good sense from the inside. From the outside it can look like a run of lucky breaks you didn't take.

At work it's the half-offer made in a corridor that you never followed up because a corridor didn't seem official enough. Socially it's the new person who suggested coffee twice before giving up. With money it's the good rate that lapsed while you compared it with three others. Next time something opens up, take the first small step within a day and leave the rest to think about later.
rising.reversed:
Turned over on a Taurus Ascendant, the steadiness people found reassuring starts to look stuck. Everything around you is moving and you're the one thing that won't, so a lucky shift passes while you're still deciding whether it's safe. Jupiter reversed can also make you complacent, sure your luck will hold without any effort, and you rest on a good moment until it quietly changes under you.

The new opportunity goes to the colleague who said yes while you were deliberating. Someone keen on you reads your slowness as lack of interest and drifts off. Your caution serves you well most of the time, and there's no need to throw it out. Catch the one opening that won't wait, answer it before you've talked yourself into waiting, and let the certainty arrive later.

sun.upright:
Jupiter has to work hard in Gemini. It's in detriment here, in the sign opposite its home, which means the Wheel's big, lucky, wide-angle way of doing things runs against the grain of a sign that likes things small, quick and plural. Mutable air, ruled by Mercury, a Gemini Sun is proud of knowing a bit about everything and being good company while it does. You've usually got five things going. The Wheel wants you to back one long arc and let it carry you, and that feels like shutting all the other doors.

You'll feel it as an opposition, because that's what it is. Sagittarius, Jupiter's own sign, sits straight across the zodiac from Gemini, and the two ends of that line are the many small facts and the one big meaning. Your gift is the facts, the quick connection, the detail nobody else caught. The luck in this card is at the far end, in the pattern that only shows up when you stay with something long enough. Jupiter also rules the first ten degrees of Gemini, the decan of the Eight of Swords, the card of feeling trapped, and that's the risk for you, so many options that none of them moves.

At work it's having five projects so you never get judged on one, when the promotion needs you to own a single thing. With money it's lots of small scattered bets and no patient one. Friends might notice you're everywhere and committed to nothing. Take the idea you keep coming back to and give it three months of proper attention.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the Wheel catches a Gemini Sun scattering the luck it's being offered. Jupiter already struggles in your sign, and reversed it turns into talk. The big break, the plan, the opportunity, spread across so many half-started threads that nothing lands. You can describe the lucky future brilliantly. That's part of the problem, because describing it feels like progress and slowly takes the place of doing it.

At work it's the string of promising starts, and the colleague who finished the one you dropped. With money it's the clever scheme talked up at dinner and never set going. The Eight of Swords sits in Jupiter's slice of Gemini, and here it's the sense of being trapped that's really just too many open options. Pick the thread you'd least like to lose and close two others on purpose. You'll feel the loss for a day or so, and then mostly relief.

moon.upright:
Gemini Moons deal with a feeling by talking about it, and most of the time that works. The Wheel complicates it. Jupiter works against the grain in Gemini, the sign of its detriment, and what it asks of your Moon is exactly what a quick mind resists, which is to sit inside a mood long enough to feel where it's going, without narrating it from the side. You've got words for every feeling you have. Having the words isn't the same as the feeling shifting.

Sagittarius sits opposite your Moon, and that axis is the whole thing in small. At your end, the running commentary, the clever read on why you feel what you feel. At the far end, a bigger sense of what it means, which usually only arrives after you've stopped talking. Pisces, the other sign Jupiter rules, squares Gemini as well, and that friction is the deeper feeling under the chatter, the one without neat words, which keeps tugging until it gets some room.

With a partner it can be the hurt you explained so well you both thought it was dealt with. It wasn't. Among friends you're always fine to talk to and rarely the one admitting you're not fine. Sleep is often the giveaway, the mind still drafting messages at one in the morning. After you've talked a feeling through, stay quiet for a full minute and notice what's still sitting there.
moon.reversed:
A Gemini Moon under the reversed Wheel gets caught in a loop. The Eight of Swords sits in Jupiter's ten degrees of Gemini, the card of feeling boxed in, and here the box is a mind that won't stop. Jupiter's already uncomfortable in your sign, and upside down it inflates the worrying, so a small feeling gets talked over and around until it's a whole anxious weather system and the actual emotion never gets a word in.

Friends get the long messages at odd hours. Work gets the scattered day where you touched everything and finished nothing. Your body gets the tight jaw and the skipped lunch. Give the restless part one job with an end to it. Write the worry out by hand on a single page, then shut the notebook and go and do something else.

rising.upright:
A Gemini Ascendant arrives mid-thought, three questions in, curious about everyone, and people read you as bright and full of possibility. The Wheel drawn on that entrance adds a sense that something's about to happen around you. The catch is that Gemini is Jupiter's sign of detriment, opposite its home, so that lucky, buoyant front takes real effort to keep pointed in one direction. You open a dozen doors in a week and the people watching can't tell which one you mean to walk through.

Sagittarius sits opposite your rising sign, and the pull toward that far end is the fix hidden in the problem. The luck is in following one opening all the way through. Pisces squares Gemini too, and you'll feel that whenever a first meeting asks for depth and your instinct is to keep it light and moving. Then there's the Eight of Swords, the decan Jupiter rules in your first ten degrees, which is the trap of having so many possible directions that you pick none and call it keeping your options open.

At work it's the business card from an event that's still in your coat pocket. In dating it's a great first evening followed by a fortnight of witty messages and no second date, each of you waiting for the other to commit. With a creative plan it's the collaborator you've enthused at three times and never sent a file. Of everything you've said you'd love to do, pick one and put a date on it.
rising.reversed:
With the Wheel reversed, a Gemini Ascendant can come across as all flicker and no follow-through. Jupiter's already awkward in your rising sign, and upside down it makes the lucky front oversell. There's big talk at a first meeting that the follow-up never matches, and people start halving whatever you say. The Eight of Swords decan shows up as a scattered, slightly stuck first impression, lots of doors pointed at and none opened.

A new manager stops asking you for time estimates because they've learned to double them. A new friend hears about a plan that was definite and then wasn't, twice. Slow the opening line right down. Say one plain, true thing about why you're there and let the pause after it stand, without filling it with three more possibilities. Then send the follow-up you promised within a day.

sun.upright:
Of all twelve Suns, Cancer gets one of the kindest versions of this card. Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, treated as an honoured guest and doing its most generous work, and the good fortune it brings arrives through the things you already lead with, care, home, family, the people you look after. Cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, you build yourself around belonging. Other signs have to chase their luck. Yours is often handed to you by people who trust you.

What a Cancer Sun has to watch is the same protectiveness that makes the luck possible. You start things for other people's sake, and you can spend a whole lucky stretch tending everyone else's good news and forget to have any of your own. Pisces, the water sign Jupiter rules, is trine to Cancer, so there's an easy flow here, a feel for an opening before anyone else can see it. Sagittarius is quincunx, five signs away with nothing in common, which is why the loud, grab-it-and-run kind of luck has never suited you. You don't need it.

At work it might be recognition that comes because people rely on you, and your habit of passing it straight on to the team. At home it's the plenty you make for everyone and rarely take a share of. With money it's the security you build for others while your own plan waits its turn. Name one thing you want out of this and take it openly, before you share the rest.
sun.reversed:
The blocked side of this for a Cancer Sun is good fortune held so protectively it can't grow. Jupiter is at its best in your sign, and reversed that generosity turns into clinging, guarding a version of home or family that life has already moved past. You give and give, and some resentment builds underneath, because the giving was meant to keep everything safe and things changed anyway.

At work it's turning down an opportunity because wanting it openly feels greedy. At home it's holding the household to a shape that suited everyone five years ago. With money it's saving against a threat that's mostly a feeling. Ask for one good thing to be yours, out loud, to the person who can give it. Then let one thing you've been protecting change in its own way.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon at home, feeling everything at full strength and needing to know the people under your roof are alright. The Wheel brings Jupiter into that, and Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, so this is a generous draw for your feelings. Moods come in wide swells. When happiness arrives it arrives big, and you might find yourself tearing up at something small and good in the supermarket queue.

Pisces is trine to your Moon, water to water, and that's real ease, a deep well of feeling and an instinct for other people's that runs almost without effort. The friction is small but it's there. Sagittarius sits quincunx to Cancer, and the part of Jupiter that wants to throw the doors open and go looking at the wide world doesn't sit easily with your need for the familiar. You'll find yourself adjusting between the two more than you'd like, wanting the trip and wanting to stay home on the same afternoon.

A partner might notice you bracing against a contentment you can't quite believe in. With your mother, or whoever did the mothering, an old feeling can come back with a new understanding attached. Your stomach and your sleep usually track your mood a day before your mind admits it. When the next low comes, let it be low for an evening, and don't make any decisions until it's passed.
moon.reversed:
An ordinary low can feel like the end of the world to a Cancer Moon with the Wheel reversed. Jupiter, so kind here upright, swells the sadness instead, until it fills the whole house and you pull into your shell. Old hurts get held close and fed. You might find yourself brooding over something said last year that nobody else remembers.

At home it's the meal cooked in pointed silence, the three-day withdrawal over something unsaid. With family it's an old wound reopened as though it were new. Your body carries it too, with appetite and sleep going first. Name the low out loud to one person you trust, and let them hear it without trying to fix it. Most of the time it starts to shift once it's been said to someone.

rising.upright:
People relax around a Cancer Ascendant. You read the mood of a room before you say much, and strangers tend to feel looked after before they know why. The Wheel on your mask is a lucky draw, because Jupiter is exalted in Cancer and does its most generous work right at the doorway of your chart. You come across as someone good things happen to and good people gather round, and doors open quietly, through warmth, without any hard pitch. Pisces is trine to your rising sign, which adds an instinct for which way a room is about to go.

The tension is between the card's readiness and your shell. The Chariot is Cancer's own Major, a driver in armour going forward, and the Wheel would like you to go forward with a bit less armour on. Sagittarius is quincunx to your Ascendant, and that awkward angle is the brash, throw-yourself-at-it kind of beginning that never feels like you. So you wait for an introduction, a reason to be there, a chance to have met everyone once already, and a good opening can drift past while you decide whether it's safe.

At work it's the role you'd be wonderful in and won't apply for cold. Socially it's the group that's invited you twice. In a new romance it's weeks of waiting for the other person to move first. When an opening asks you to step forward before you feel ready, step anyway while people are warm to you. You can always go back into your shell afterwards.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the Wheel can make a Cancer Ascendant changeable at the door, warm one day and unreachable the next, so new people can't tell which version they'll meet. Jupiter is exalted in your sign, and upside down that can turn into over-protecting, reading a harmless newcomer as a threat and shutting the shell. Or you polish a lucky first impression that the follow-through can't quite hold. Either way the opening stalls while you wait to feel safe enough to take it.

A new colleague takes the quiet for disapproval when it's shyness. Someone you like reads your retreat after a lovely evening as lost interest and moves on. Feeling safe may not arrive before the chance does. Pick one new person and tell them, in a sentence, what you're hoping for, and send it before you've reread it five times.

sun.upright:
The Six of Wands sits inside Leo, in the ten degrees Jupiter rules, and it's the card of riding home to applause. So when the Wheel lands on a Leo Sun, the luck it brings tends to be the visible kind. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you want to be seen doing the thing you're proud of, and this is a turn that puts you in view. Jupiter holds no rank in Leo and takes its tone from the Sun, your own ruler, so the good fortune comes warm and a little theatrical, and other people notice it happening to you.

Sagittarius, Jupiter's fire sign, is trine to Leo, which is why this can feel so easy. The tension is in what you do once you're up there. A Leo Sun can want the applause so much it tries to make one good moment permanent, telling the same story of the same triumph long after it's done its job, and the Wheel doesn't stop for anybody. Pisces is quincunx to Leo, and that awkward angle is the quiet, behind-the-scenes way of doing things. It isn't your instinct. The next part of this may ask for it anyway.

At work it's the project that lifts your standing, and your urge to keep talking about it for a year. With something creative, the piece that landed well tempts you to make it again. In love it's a warm stretch enjoyed so loudly you forget to let it deepen. Take the credit gladly, then start the next thing before the applause has quite died down.
sun.reversed:
A lucky streak can turn into a show for a Leo Sun. Reversed, Jupiter under the Sun inflates it, so you announce the win before it's solid, or keep taking bows for something that finished months ago. Underneath is a worry that if the applause stops you stop mattering, and that makes it hard to let a good phase quietly become the next one.

At work it's a reputation running a little ahead of what you've actually delivered, and the private worry about that gap. In love it's needing the relationship to look lucky to other people, whatever it feels like from inside. The Six of Wands decan can go sour here, into chasing applause for its own sake. Do one good piece of work nobody will see, and don't mention it to anyone.

moon.upright:
Leo Moons need to feel chosen. Warmly noticed, picked out of a crowd, missed when they're not there. The Wheel says your inner weather is swinging toward exactly that kind of warmth. Jupiter comes into Leo without any rank of its own and borrows the Sun's heat, so feelings run in big bright colours and a good day floods you. Sagittarius is trine to your Moon, fire to fire, and that's why your optimism comes back so quickly after a low.

The rub is pride, and pace. Fixed fire holds a feeling for a long time, a warmth or a hurt, and the Wheel keeps moving. Admitting that something small wounded you, a forgotten message, a party you weren't asked to, can feel beneath you, so you complain grandly about something else and the real feeling sits there untouched. Pisces sits quincunx to your Moon, the awkward angle, and it stands for the quiet, soft, needy feeling that doesn't match your usual bright register. You'd rather not make room for it, and you'll probably have to.

Your partner may get the row about the dishes that's really about not being looked at properly all week. With friends you're the generous host who then lies awake counting who didn't say thank you. The body runs hot as well, and sleep comes late. Say the small, true version of the hurt to one person, in about ten words.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, a Leo Moon wants an audience for its feelings and then resents the audience. Jupiter under the Sun makes a fine story of every hurt, told well and told often, and the telling slowly replaces the feeling it was about. Or the pride slams it all shut and you go bright and busy and fine, and nobody, including the people who could help, is allowed near the sore spot.

Friends notice the same story has done the rounds three times, with small improvements each time. A partner notices you're sunny with everyone except them. Sleep goes shallow. If one person actually hurt you, tell that person the plain version once, then stop retelling it, and watch how quickly the feeling starts to move once it isn't being performed.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks in as though it was expected. Warm, a bit of theatre, someone who'll lift the evening. The Sun rules your chart, and with the Wheel on your mask the entrance picks up a lucky glow, so people warm to you before you've proved anything. Jupiter is only a guest in Leo, lit by the Sun, and Sagittarius is trine to your Ascendant, fire meeting fire, so that shine and your natural confidence pull the same way and doors open on the strength of it.

The Six of Wands sits in the middle of Leo, Jupiter's own ten degrees, the card of arriving to applause, and first impressions really do tend to go your way. The complication is that fixed fire likes a reliable act. You'll run the entrance you know works even when the moment wants something rougher and more real. Pisces, five signs from Leo, is the mismatch, the softer, unguarded way of meeting people that never quite feels like your style.

At an interview it's the charm that carries the first round and the harder question in the second that charm can't answer. On a first date it's two lovely hours in which neither of you says anything true. In a new team you're liked quickly and trusted slowly. Next time you meet someone, skip the line you know always lands and ask them something you actually want to know.
rising.reversed:
Flipped, a Leo Ascendant can promise more at the door than the follow-through delivers. Jupiter lit by the Sun, reversed, oversells the entrance, the big warm confidence that wins the room and then leaves people waiting for what it implied. Or the nerve deserts you and you run the act on autopilot, smiling with nobody home, hoping the gap doesn't show.

At work it's the pitch that dazzled the client and the colleague now quietly stuck delivering it. Socially it's being the life of the night and going home feeling oddly unseen. The Six of Wands decan can tip into needing the applause more than the thing you're applauded for. For a while, promise a little under what you can do at any first meeting, and let people find the rest for themselves.

sun.upright:
Jupiter is in detriment in Virgo. It's the sign opposite Pisces, one of Jupiter's homes, and the planet has to work against the grain here with the effort showing. For a Virgo Sun that's most of the story. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you build yourself on being useful and getting it right, and the Wheel's way of working is broad, lucky and a bit careless with detail. The good fortune is real. It just arrives asking you to trust a pattern you can't check line by line, and trusting what you can't check isn't your favourite thing.

Pisces sits opposite Virgo, and that axis is the lesson. Your end is the careful particular, the flaw spotted, the plan tightened. The far end is faith, letting something imperfect go out because the timing's right. Sagittarius squares Virgo too, Jupiter's fire sign pressing on yours, friction that forces the issue, and it usually turns up as a chance that won't wait while you polish. I've seen plenty of Virgo Suns miss a good year this way, still refining the thing they were meant to send months ago.

At work it's the opportunity you nearly lose because you're still perfecting the draft. With money it's the sensible budget where the one bet on yourself keeps getting cut for being unproven. Your health routine might be the same, optimised endlessly and kept inconsistently. Send one good thing out at ninety per cent, and don't reopen it.
sun.reversed:
All of a Virgo Sun's skill can end up aimed at what's wrong, and none of it at what could be. Jupiter's already strained in your sign, and with the card reversed it turns you into the critic who makes nothing. You edit everyone else's work and keep a private list of your own mistakes running late into the night. It can feel like being responsible. Mostly it's a way of never being the one on the hook.

At work it's fixing a colleague's email while your own project sits untouched for a month. At home it's the partner who's stopped asking for help because the help comes back with corrections. Pisces, the sign across from yours, is about letting things be, and you could use a little of that. Go a whole day correcting nothing, yourself included, and put the saved energy into one unfinished thing of your own.

moon.upright:
When a Virgo Moon is upset, something usually gets cleaned. Mercury rules Virgo, and you settle a feeling by being useful, sorting a drawer, answering the emails, fixing whatever can be fixed. The Wheel brings a change that tidying won't control. Jupiter is in detriment in Virgo, so the card's big, trusting way of letting a feeling pass sits awkwardly with a Moon that likes to manage things down to size.

Sagittarius squares your Moon, and that friction is the restlessness under the neatness. The checking. The list you run through at midnight. The sense that if you get everything right the anxiety will finally stop. It won't, to be honest, and knowing why you're upset doesn't finish the feeling any more than a clean kitchen does. Pisces, opposite, is the missing half, a trust that moods come and go without you supervising them.

The body usually shows it first, a tight stomach, broken sleep, skin that flares up. A partner might find you sorting out their admin and never mentioning you were lonely. In the family you may still be the good, useful one, so nobody has to worry about you. When you catch yourself tidying for the second time in a day, stop and leave one thing undone.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, tidying stops working for a Virgo Moon, and the worry gets itself a job title. Jupiter, uncomfortable in your sign, starts auditing every feeling. Was that reaction reasonable? Is this tiredness something serious? Did they mean it that way? There's a great deal of thinking and almost no comfort in it, and the routines that usually settle you start to feel like tests you keep failing.

Sleep tends to go first, then digestion, then your patience with the people you love. A partner hears the fifth question about the same small thing and runs out of answers. Take one routine and do it deliberately badly for a week, the unmade bed, the unplanned lunch, the email sent without a second read, and notice that nothing falls apart.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising notices things. The typo, your shoes, the nearest exit, and people pick up on that care and read you as composed and a little reserved. Put the Wheel on that front and the openings coming your way are lucky ones, which is slightly awkward, because Jupiter is in detriment on this Ascendant. Luck doesn't sit naturally in your hands. Your instinct at the start of anything is to check it for faults, and the card wants you to step through before you've verified every part. People already trust you to be accurate. This asks them to trust you with a chance.

Sagittarius squares your rising sign, and you'll feel that as the pitch you'd love to make and immediately want to edit, the idea held back until it's watertight. Pisces opposite is the counterweight, a faith that a rough beginning can still be a good one. The luck here rarely arrives finished, and that's exactly what a careful Ascendant finds hard to say yes to.

In a new role it's the admin handed to you in week one that you're still doing in year three, because reliable is the impression you give. In a friendship you might be the dependable one who never gets rung for fun. Buying something big, it's the clause you spotted that saved everyone money and nobody thanked you for. In the next meeting, put your idea on the table before your correction.
rising.reversed:
Flipped, a Virgo Ascendant can go stiff at first contact. The accuracy that usually reassures people reads as coolness or fuss, because Jupiter, awkward in your rising sign, spends its effort avoiding mistakes and forgets to reach the person in front of you. You might hear yourself correcting someone you've only just met, or go so careful you say almost nothing and let them fill the silence with guesses.

A new manager takes your questions for doubt. A date takes the precision for judgement. Fair or not, that's how it lands. Let a small mistake stand in a message without fixing it, or tell a story that isn't quite finished, and see whether anyone minds. Usually nobody does, and the conversation gets warmer for it.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns weigh things. Cardinal air, ruled by Venus, you want life fair and pleasant, you'd like to be liked while you arrange it, and you're very good at seeing both sides. The Wheel brings a lucky turn, and it needs a decision from you. Jupiter is only a visitor in Libra and takes its cue from Venus, so the luck comes graciously, through people and charm and a connection that opens a door. Sagittarius, a sign Jupiter rules, is sextile to Libra, a cooperative angle that only pays off if you actually pick it up.

The tension is timing. The Wheel asks you to move while the chance is there, and Libra likes to consult. Justice is your Major, and it's worth remembering she holds a sword as well as the scales. At some point the weighing ends and something gets cut. Jupiter also rules the last ten degrees of Libra, the decan of the Four of Swords, a figure lying still on a tomb, and in a Libra Sun that rest can become a very graceful way of putting off a decision. Pisces is five signs from Libra, a quincunx, and you might feel that as a suspicion that the fair choice and the lucky one aren't the same, so you keep adjusting between them and choose neither.

At work it's the good offer that needs a yes while you're still checking nobody's put out by it. In love, a lucky shift gets met by asking what everyone else wants first. Make the decision you've been politely stalling on and tell the people it affects.
sun.reversed:
Charm turns into a hiding place for a Libra Sun with this card upside down. Jupiter under Venus is lovely company and very good at telling people what they want to hear, and the cost arrives later, in the agreement you didn't mean and the favour you'll resent. Over months it adds up, and people end up fond of you without quite knowing what you think about anything.

At work it's being agreeable in the meeting and privately annoyed at the outcome. In a relationship it's the resentment that seems to come from nowhere and has actually been saved up since last year. The Four of Swords decan lets it all rest quietly for far too long. Find one honest thing you've been smoothing over to keep the peace, and say the whole of it, gently.

moon.upright:
Discord gets into a Libra Moon's body. If two people you love aren't getting on, you feel it in your shoulders before you've worked out why. Venus rules Libra, and what you need is peace, more exactly everyone around you on decent terms. The Wheel says that balance is shifting. Jupiter comes in as Venus's guest with no rank of its own, so it moves your feelings gently, through relationships and fairness. Sagittarius is sextile to your Moon, and that's the easy opening, a warmth that helps you talk two people back together, including you and whoever you've fallen out with.

Talking a feeling into something reasonable can talk it clean out of existence, though. You're so good at seeing the other person's side that by the time you understand them there's no room left for your own hurt. Pisces, quincunx to Libra, is the mismatch, a body that keeps hold of a feeling after your mind has fairly explained it away. The leftover turns up later as a headache or a flat afternoon.

Your partner has probably noticed you're always the one who moves first to smooth things over, asking nothing back. In the group chat you're the peacekeeper, reading every message twice for tone. And your body pays for it, a heavy tiredness after even nice social things, from all that invisible balancing. Next time you're annoyed, stay annoyed for an hour before you work out why they did it.
moon.reversed:
A Libra Moon can find itself negotiating its own feelings. Reversed, Jupiter under Venus keeps hunting for the fair version, the right tone, the reply that upsets nobody, and you end up drafting an emotion instead of having it. Or you can't tell what you feel at all, because every feeling seems to need someone else's approval before it's allowed in the room.

With a partner it's asking what they want five times and being quietly cross at the answer. With friends it's the message rewritten so often it doesn't say anything anymore, still sitting unsent. Your shoulders carry the tension after a perfectly nice visit. When someone next asks how you are, give a short true answer and don't soften it with a joke.

rising.upright:
Libra rising makes a first meeting look easy. You arrive graceful and easy to talk to, the one who makes the introductions and remembers everyone's name, and people come away from a first conversation with you feeling understood. The Wheel drawn here says first meetings are turning your way. Jupiter is only a guest in Libra, but Sagittarius, Jupiter's own fire sign, is sextile to your rising sign, so the card's lucky reach and your social ease pull together, and new contacts respond to it.

Libra is cardinal air, a sign built for starting things, and the Wheel wants you to start. Your instinct at the door is to mirror. You match the other person's pace, their tone, sometimes their opinions, and it works so well you can lose track of what you came in to say. Pisces is quincunx to Libra, and you'll feel that as a faint dissonance, the moment you sense your own view is different from theirs and smooth it over before it shows.

In a negotiation it's the deal that felt friendly and left you with less than you meant to accept. On a first date it's being so tuned to them that they learn nothing about you. Starting a new job, you're well liked from day one and consulted on nothing that matters. Before your next meeting with someone new, decide one thing you want from it and say it in the first ten minutes.
rising.reversed:
Turned over, a Libra Ascendant can come off as all surface. Jupiter in Venus's sign turns the charm up and the substance down, and people leave a first meeting having liked you and unsure what you actually said. You may be handing each person the version of you they'll like best, which is tiring to keep up and tends to catch up with you the moment two of those people compare notes.

At work it's two colleagues discovering you agreed with both of them. Socially it's the invitations you accepted out of politeness and now can't face. At the next introduction, say one thing you actually think that the other person might disagree with. Say it calmly, and let them disagree.

sun.upright:
Up in the top corner of the card there's an eagle, a book open in front of it, watching the wheel go round. That's roughly how a Scorpio Sun would like to meet a change of fortune, from a height, having read everything first. Fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, you build yourself on depth and on not being fooled. The Wheel brings a turn you can't fully investigate before it arrives, which is an odd test for you.

Jupiter has no dignity in Scorpio and takes its colour from Mars, so the luck here comes deep and a bit fated, closer to a change in your life than a windfall. Pisces, Jupiter's other home, is trine to Scorpio, water to water, and that's the real gift, a sense of which way things are moving before anyone else feels it. The strain is between the card's openness and your instinct to keep your cards close. The Wheel lays fortune out on the table, and you'd prefer nobody saw the table. Sagittarius sits next door to Scorpio, a neighbour with little in common, and its breezy it'll-all-work-out attitude never quite fits a sign that likes to know exactly what it's dealing with.

At work it's an opportunity that needs you to let go of a plan you've been quietly controlling. In love it's a deepening you can feel coming and brace against. With shared money you'd sooner steer the change than go with it. Let one good thing happen without managing it, and keep a note of what that actually costs you.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, a Scorpio Sun can start using what it knows as leverage. Jupiter coloured by Mars gets tactical in your sign, and upside down it keeps a lucky break to itself for later. Information sat on until it can win something. A change others aren't told about. It works, often well, and it leaves you alone with what you know in a way that's hard to admit.

At work it's the opening you kept quiet until it could pay off, and the trust that drained away once people noticed. In love it's a memory for every wrong, filed and dated. With money, it can be an account or a debt your partner doesn't know about. Take one thing you've been holding in reserve and hand it plainly to someone who'd be glad of it.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel everything at full depth and trust very few people with any of it. Fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern charts Pluto, you need loyalty, privacy and the truth, roughly in that order. The Wheel brings a change in how you feel that's bigger than you'd normally allow. Jupiter comes into Scorpio as a guest of Mars with no dignity of its own, and what it offers is a widening, feelings that won't fit in the usual locked box. Pisces, trine to Scorpio and water like it, is what makes that bearable, a depth that can carry a big feeling without going under.

The rub is control. The Wheel asks you to let a feeling change you on its own schedule, and a Scorpio Moon likes to decide exactly who sees what, and when. Sagittarius sits next to Scorpio, semi-sextile, and its everything-happens-for-a-reason optimism lands badly on a Moon that learned early to expect the undertow. You don't need blind faith. You need to let one deep feeling move at its own pace without gripping it.

There may be something you've never told a partner, about what a certain silence of theirs does to you. In the family it's the old thing nobody names, and the relief when one person finally does. At night your dreams can get vivid, your mind turning things over while you sleep. Tell the person you trust most one true thing you've never said out loud, and keep it short.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, a Scorpio Moon takes its feelings underground. Jupiter under Mars turns inward and starts interpreting, reading every message for the thing hidden in it, sure it knows what's going on in someone else's head and never checking. The feeling wants to move and the grip won't let it.

It can show as a jealousy that won't be argued with, or a silence at home that everyone feels and nobody names. Sleep goes restless and the three-in-the-morning thoughts get very convincing. Pisces, trine to your Moon, is the part of you that can feel something without needing to control it. Ask one direct question about the thing you've been interpreting, and take the answer at face value for a week before you decide what it really meant.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising doesn't give much away. People meeting you feel watched, in a way that isn't unfriendly, and they often feel read before they've said anything. Mars rules your chart, with Pluto as its modern co-ruler. With the Wheel on your mask, the openings you get when you start something are lucky ones, and they come as a quiet pull, people drawn to you without knowing why. Jupiter is only a guest in Scorpio, but Pisces, which it rules, is trine to your Ascendant, and that gives you an instinct for which way a room is about to move.

What pulls against it is that this card likes the open hand, fortune out on show, and a Scorpio Ascendant shows nothing until it's sure. Sagittarius is the awkward neighbour, semi-sextile to Scorpio, the loud, sunny way of starting that never feels like yours and that a lucky moment sometimes asks for anyway. So your first meetings split. When you decide to show a little, they go remarkably well. When you stay behind the glass, people leave slightly nervous of you and don't say so.

In an interview it's the short, exact answer that unsettles the panel. In dating it's the intensity people find magnetic in the first hour and hard work by the third date if nothing opens up. At a new workplace it's the formidable reputation you earn in week one by saying very little. Offer one ordinary personal thing early, your weekend, a book, the town you grew up in.
rising.reversed:
Reserve can tip into suspicion for a Scorpio Ascendant with the Wheel reversed. Jupiter under Mars reads every newcomer for their motive, and people can feel themselves being weighed from the moment they sit down. Or you give off a charge you don't intend, and your silence gets taken for judgement when it's really caution.

At work it's new colleagues keeping their distance, and you reading that distance as proof they're hiding something. In friendship it's testing people before you let them in, and losing the good ones who don't enjoy being tested. Pisces, trine to your rising sign, gives you a gentler way of reading a room if you let it. At the next first meeting, say what you honestly think of the conversation you're in, a little sooner than feels comfortable.

sun.upright:
Jupiter rules Sagittarius, so with a Sagittarius Sun this card is on home ground. The planet is in its own sign, strong and unforced, and you already live the way the Wheel describes, trusting that things tend to work out if you keep going. Mutable fire, you're here to find out what it all means and say so out loud, and this draw widens a horizon you were already looking at. A lucky break can feel almost ordinary to you, like the weather you grew up in.

When the card's planet is your sign's own ruler, it's pointing at your gift and asking you to use it on purpose. Your faith that it'll work out is real, and it does pull opportunities toward you. The catch is aim. Pisces, the water sign Jupiter also rules, squares Sagittarius and insists that a big vision needs a small next step or it stays a lovely idea. Temperance is your sign's Major, an angel patiently pouring water from one cup into another, and patience with the dull middle is what this asks of you. Sagittarius Suns can trust their luck so completely they forget to be standing anywhere in particular when it arrives.

At work it's the sweeping plan that would fly if somebody did the boring middle part. With study or travel it's the horizon you talk about and haven't booked. In love it might be the big, honest promise, made sincerely and never costed. Take the vision you mention most often and do the first ordinary step before you tell anyone else about it.
sun.reversed:
The vision runs out ahead of the work for a Sagittarius Sun, and you can talk a very good game. Jupiter reversed in its own sign becomes the sweeping claim with nothing under it, the plan that's mostly enthusiasm, the story that grows a bit each time it's told. You believe it while you're saying it, which is exactly why other people believe it too, for a while.

At work it's the big announcements that now get a polite nod and no questions. With friends it's the trip you've all been planning for three years. In love it's a future described beautifully without a single step taken toward it. Pisces squares your sign and keeps asking for something real. Pick one thing you've said you'll do, and either do the first part of it or say out loud that you won't.

moon.upright:
Give a Sagittarius Moon some room and something to look forward to and it'll cope with nearly anything. You need to feel that life is bigger than this week. The Wheel sits comfortably in that, because Jupiter rules Sagittarius, so the card is at home in your feelings, and your instinct that a low will lift is usually right. You feel things hugely, find the meaning in them, and want to get going again.

The part worth watching is that you skip straight to the meaning. Pisces squares your Moon, water on fire, pointing at the specific feeling under the philosophy, the actual hurt you've already turned into a lesson. A mood handled only as a lesson comes back as restlessness. The sudden urge to book a flight or quit something is usually a particular feeling that never got felt.

Partners tend to notice it first. You're cheerful about a problem that's clearly bothering you, and you want space the second the conversation gets detailed. Friends know you as the one who's always up for an adventure, and hard to reach when things are dull or sad. Your body wants to move and walk it off. So walk it off, and on the way back, name to yourself the exact moment that set it going.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, Jupiter at home in a Sagittarius Moon takes a feeling and turns it into a speech. You know what you ought to feel, you've got the philosophy ready, and the actual fear or hurt sits unattended underneath. Or the restlessness takes over, and you keep moving so you never have to look at it.

At home it's plans changed at short notice, fresh starts, a partner who's tired of never knowing where you'll be. With friends it's the funny version of a bad week, told so well that nobody asks how you really are. Sleep can go patchy when you're avoiding something. Before the next big change, sit for ten minutes and say plainly what you're trying to get away from, out loud if you can.

rising.upright:
Friendly, a bit loud, ready for anything, that's how most people meet a Sagittarius Ascendant, and they take to it quickly. Jupiter rules your rising sign, so the Wheel is at home on this Ascendant. The card's own planet is standing at your front door, and you really do read as someone luck travels with. Openings arrive on the strength of your optimism, and they're yours to work with, since the planet handing them out is your chart ruler.

The complication is aim. Pisces squares your Ascendant, and you'll feel that friction at the start of things, in the way you'd sooner leap in than read the terms, and tend to find out the details after you've said yes. That can charm people. It can also leave you promising the earth at a first meeting and privately dreading the follow-up. Doors swing open because you're warm and quick. Whether people back you a second time depends on whether the first thing got finished.

In a new job it's the energy everyone loves in week one and the unanswered emails by week six. When you travel, it's the booking made in a rush with a condition you didn't read. In a new friendship it's the wonderful plan proposed on impulse, and the other person waiting to see if you meant it. Before you say yes to the next big thing, ask one practical question, even if it takes the shine off the moment a little.
rising.reversed:
First impressions get unreliable for a Sagittarius Ascendant with the Wheel reversed. The big easy talk that usually opens doors comes out as bluster or tactlessness, and Jupiter at home here, upside down, blurts the blunt thing in the wrong company. Or you overpromise so warmly that people are let down later by the ordinary size of what you can actually do.

At work it's the client who remembers your promise better than you do. Socially it's the joke that went down badly with someone you'd only just met, and the apology you never quite made. On a first date it can be the big talk about travel plans you haven't actually made. Slow the first five minutes down. Ask a question, hear the whole answer, and promise nothing until the second conversation, however much you'd like to.

sun.upright:
Jupiter is in fall in Capricorn. It's uncomfortable there, a bit unheard, and has to find an indirect way to do its job, so for a Capricorn Sun the Wheel's luck doesn't drop in your lap the way it might for a fire sign. Cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, you build yourself through achievement and the long climb, and you'd like to be respected for what you built. Good fortune here comes as an opening you have to recognise and then work, which, to be fair, is how you prefer things anyway.

Pisces, one of Jupiter's homes, is sextile to Capricorn, a cooperative angle and a real help, softness and chance meeting your patience halfway. Jupiter also rules the first ten degrees of your sign, the decan of the Two of Pentacles, a young man juggling two coins and still dancing. That's the good version of this luck, fortune that comes from keeping several things going and staying light on your feet. The tension is that you distrust anything that comes too easily. If a door is simply open, you'll often assume there's a catch and go the hard way round.

At work it's a break that comes through a relationship, and your suspicion of it because you didn't sweat for it. With money it's the sensible plan with no room in it for one lighter bet. With a parent or a boss, you may still be trying to earn approval with results. Let one good thing in through the side door, and say thank you for it.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun can go cold and calculating with the luck it's offered. Jupiter in fall, upside down, measures people for their usefulness and treats every break as a deal to be won, and the warmth drains out of it. Or the opposite happens. The tools stay in the box because you've decided you're not senior enough to use them yet, and you wait for a permission that isn't coming.

At work it's answering emails late into the evening because that feels safer than reaching for the opening in front of you. With friends it's the catch-up postponed until things calm down, which they never quite do. Do one thing you'd already be doing if you had the title you're working toward.

moon.upright:
There's a snake sliding down the left-hand side of this card, and a Capricorn Moon will usually look at it first and assume that's the bit meant for them. Saturn rules Capricorn, and a Saturn Moon feels safe when it's in control and has proved it can cope. You prepare for the drop. Jupiter is in fall in your sign, so the card's easy faith that things will come round doesn't come naturally, and feelings are something you'd prefer to deal with by doing something practical.

That practicality is genuinely wise, and the Pisces sextile helps, a softness that lets some trust in without you having to force it. The friction is that you treat needing anyone as a weakness, and a lucky turn often arrives through leaning on someone, which you hate. Jupiter rules the Two of Pentacles decan at the start of Capricorn, and it describes the balancing act you're already doing, holding it all together for everyone while privately sure the luck belongs to other people.

The people closest to you often don't know you're struggling until it's serious, because you cope so well. In the family you're probably still the reliable one who never gets looked after. Physically it's the tension of always bracing, the jaw, the shoulders, a sleep that stays half on duty. Let one person do one real thing for you, and don't pay them back straight away.
moon.reversed:
Flipped, a Capricorn Moon braces for a fall that may not come. Jupiter in fall, reversed, hardens the pessimism, so an ordinary low reads as proof the luck was never real and you shut down into grim self-reliance, sure that asking for help would only prove you couldn't cope. The feeling wants to lift and you've decided in advance it won't.

With a partner it's the wall that goes up exactly when you most need holding. At work it's taking on more to feel in control when you're already tired. In the body it's the exhaustion of carrying it alone, and a sleep that won't switch off. Tell one person the plain truth of how you're doing, no solution attached, and let them just hear it.

rising.upright:
Even at fifteen, a Capricorn Ascendant tends to look like the one in charge. Saturn rules your chart, and people read you as serious, capable and plainly in command of yourself. With the Wheel drawn on your mask, the openings you get when you start something are lucky ones, though they come by a slower road. Jupiter is in fall on this Ascendant, so a lucky, easy front isn't your natural style. People tend to see you as someone who's earned things, and a good break usually reaches you because your competence got noticed. The Pisces sextile softens that, a friendly angle that lets some warmth and chance through the reserve.

The complication is timing. A Capricorn Ascendant likes to be sure before it moves, and the Wheel rewards stepping forward while the moment's there. Jupiter rules the Two of Pentacles decan in your first ten degrees, the knack of keeping several things in the air at once, and that's your best way in. Stay nimble. Waiting for the single perfect, certain moment is how the chance goes by. Sagittarius is semi-sextile to Capricorn, and its breezy confidence never quite fits you, which is fine.

In a new job it's the responsibility handed to you early and the promotion that comes late because you never pushed. In a friendship you're the steady one people rely on and rarely think to spoil. On a big purchase it's the shrewd move made a touch too cautiously. Say yes to the next opening while it's there, and let your thoroughness catch up afterwards.
rising.reversed:
On a Capricorn Ascendant, the reversed Wheel makes the guard read as cold. Jupiter in fall, upside down, stiffens it further, so the competent front looks unapproachable and people assume you don't need anything from them, including the opening they might have offered. Or you hang back from a chance, certain you haven't earned the right to it yet.

A new colleague takes the reserve for disinterest and stops trying. Someone who likes you reads the seriousness as a closed door. Pisces, sextile to your rising sign, is the warmth you can let show without losing any authority. Next time you meet someone new, say one human, off-duty thing about yourself early, a bad film you love, a disastrous holiday, and let people see there's a way in.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns tend to live slightly in the future. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn traditionally and Uranus in modern charts, you build yourself around ideas and principles and the people you'd stand next to at a protest, and you want to be useful to something bigger than yourself. The Wheel brings a lucky turn, and it'll most likely arrive through other people, the network, the group, the friend of a friend. Jupiter is neither helped nor hindered in Aquarius and takes its tone from Saturn, so the luck has some order to it, an opening inside a system or an organisation, only rarely a random windfall. Sagittarius, one of Jupiter's own signs, is sextile to Aquarius, a cooperative angle that pays off if you act on it.

The tension is detachment. Fixed air can hold an idea of how things ought to go and quietly refuse the turn that actually comes because it doesn't match the principle. The Wheel doesn't care whether the luck is ideologically tidy. It just wants you to take it. The Star is Aquarius's own Major, a card of hope, and hope comes easily to you in the abstract and less easily when it lands in your own lap. Pisces sits next door, semi-sextile, and it's the personal, feeling side of good fortune that your cooler head tends to skip.

At work it's the opportunity that comes through a friend, and your urge to prove you didn't need the help. In a community group it's the shared win you're slow to let benefit you personally. Take your share of the next good thing that comes through other people.
sun.reversed:
Turned the wrong way, the Wheel lets an Aquarius Sun keep a good break at arm's length. Jupiter under Saturn over-thinks the luck, holding out for the opening that fits your principles exactly while the imperfect, real one goes past. Or detachment tips into a lofty sense that you don't need what other people are reaching for. It reads as cool, and it costs you the very connections the luck was travelling through.

At work it's the collaboration turned down because it wasn't pure enough, and the solo slog that follows. With friends it's being everyone's clever adviser and nobody's easy company. In love it can look like analysing someone's interest in you until they wander off. Say yes to one thing that comes through other people, even if it's messier than you'd like.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon feels safest with a little distance. Room to think a feeling through at arm's length, friends who don't crowd you, a kind of belonging that doesn't cost your independence. The Wheel brings an emotional change that asks you to feel it more directly than you'd like. Jupiter, coloured by Saturn in your sign, moves your feelings in a measured, almost principled way. You understand a mood well before you let it touch you.

Sagittarius is sextile to your Moon, and that's the easy opening, warmth and optimism that come through friends and shared ideas and genuinely lift you. The friction is Pisces, semi-sextile, the tender, unreasoned feeling that has nothing in common with your cool understanding and keeps asking to be let in. You can explain exactly why you feel something and stay completely dry-eyed about it. The feeling tends to wait, patiently, for you to actually have it.

In a relationship you'll want space exactly when closeness is on offer, and call the retreat independence. Among friends you're the wise, unflappable one, rarely the one who admits needing anything. When feeling builds with nowhere to go, your body gets wired and nervy and sleep suffers. Let one person close while the feeling is still fresh, before you've tidied it into a theory.
moon.reversed:
An Aquarius Moon under the reversed Wheel retreats into its head. Jupiter under Saturn turns feeling into analysis, so you watch your own mood from a safe distance and never quite climb into it, sure that understanding a feeling is the same as dealing with it. Nothing moves, because you're studying it and not living it.

With a partner it's the calm, reasonable tone that leaves them lonely, unsure you're really in the room. In the body it's the wired, detached feeling of running on nerves and too much coffee. With friends it's giving great advice about their lives and changing the subject whenever yours comes up. Let yourself feel one thing messily, without explaining it, and tell someone while it's still raw.

rising.upright:
The first thing strangers notice about an Aquarius Ascendant is that you don't quite run with the crowd. Friendly, a bit detached, a bit original. Saturn rules your chart in the old system, Uranus in the new. With the Wheel on your mask, the openings coming your way are lucky ones, and they tend to come through unexpected people. Jupiter is a visitor in Aquarius, taking its manner from Saturn, so the luck at the start of things has an oddness to it, a chance that arrives sideways, through a network or a coincidence. Sagittarius is sextile to your rising sign, and your wide circle keeps handing you doors if you'll walk through them.

The complication is that fixed air likes to keep a cool, consistent front, and the Wheel sometimes asks you to be warmer at the door than your style finds comfortable. Pisces is semi-sextile to Aquarius, the neighbour with little in common, the personal, feeling way of meeting someone that you tend to hold at a slight remove. People find you interesting quickly and get close slowly, and a good opening can be waiting on the other side of that reserve.

At work it could be the unconventional role that suits you exactly, found through a friend of a friend. In a new group you're liked as the interesting one and kept a bit at arm's length. In dating it's the connection that needs you to drop the cool a notch. Meeting someone new, let some genuine warmth show early, before the detachment sets the tone.
rising.reversed:
Aloof is how an Aquarius Ascendant can come across with the Wheel reversed. Jupiter under Saturn cools the front even further, so people read you as uninterested or hard to reach and don't offer the opening they might have. Or you keep things so deliberately unconventional that a straightforward good break gets waved off as too ordinary for you.

A new colleague takes the detachment for disapproval. At work you can get left off the project you'd have loved, because nobody thought you'd care. Someone who likes you can't tell whether you're interested and gives up guessing. Sagittarius, a friendly sextile away, is the easy warmth that comes to you through people, and you keep overlooking it. At the next first meeting, drop the cool for a minute, say something plainly glad, and notice who steps closer.

sun.upright:
Jupiter is the traditional ruler of Pisces, so for a Pisces Sun this card comes from the sign's own landlord. The planet is in its own sign, strong and unforced, and you already trust the current the way the Wheel describes, sensing that life will carry you if you don't fight it. Mutable water, you're here to feel your way into the bigger picture, and a lucky turn can feel almost inevitable when it comes, as if you'd known.

With the card's planet ruling your sign, it points straight at your gift, the openness that lets good fortune find you. The catch is direction. Sagittarius, the other sign Jupiter rules, squares Pisces, fire pressing on water, and that friction says all that receptive faith needs one deliberate act or it drifts. Jupiter also rules the middle ten degrees of Pisces, the decan of the Nine of Cups, the wish card, so this turn really does lean toward contentment, as long as you reach for it. The Moon is your sign's own Major, a card of half-light and uncertain roads, and it's a fair warning that a daydream about the good thing can feel so real you forget to go and get it.

At work it's the opportunity that floats toward you and floats away again because you didn't quite act. In creative life it's the gift that needs a deadline to become a thing. In love it's the good change you can feel coming and wait for passively. Trust the current, then do the one concrete thing it's carrying you toward.
sun.reversed:
The current turns into drift for a Pisces Sun. Jupiter reversed in its own sign tips into wishful waiting, the lucky future felt so vividly it seems half-arrived, a daydream of rescue that saves you doing the small real thing. Or the faith sours into a sense that fortune has forgotten you, and you go passive and let the current take you anywhere.

At work it's the opening you sensed and never reached for, gone to someone who moved. In creative life it's the beautiful idea that stays an idea. The Nine of Cups decan can slide into a comfort that dulls the wanting. Name the thing you actually want, in one sentence, and take a single concrete step toward it before the day's out.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon picks up the feelings of everyone in the room and often can't tell which ones are its own. You settle by softening, music, water, a long bath, sleep, letting the day drain out of you. Jupiter rules Pisces, so the Wheel sits at home in your inner weather, and your instinct that a low will pass is sound. The tide does come back in.

The part to watch is that you can drift with it so completely you lose your own shape. Sagittarius squares your Moon, fire on water, and asks for one clear boundary, one feeling you can name as yours, or you take on everyone else's weather and call it your mood. The Nine of Cups decan in the middle of Pisces is the contentment on offer here, a real ease when you let a good stretch fill you up without dissolving into it.

Living with someone, you can absorb their bad day so completely you lose your own footing. Crowds leave you wrung out without knowing why. A lot of your processing happens in sleep and dreams, and you need regular time alone to come back to yourself. When the next big feeling arrives, ask whose it is before you let it carry you.
moon.reversed:
A Pisces Moon can dissolve into a low with this card upside down. Jupiter at home, reversed, swells a passing sadness until it fills everything and you slip under, reaching for the escape, the scroll, the drink, the long sleep, anything that blunts the edges. The tide wants to turn and you've stopped believing it will.

With a partner it's going vague and unreachable, there in body and gone somewhere else. In the body it's the heaviness of too much sleep that doesn't restore anything, and the days blurring into each other. Sagittarius squares your Moon and wants one firm handhold. Name the feeling as yours, say it plainly to one person, and let being specific give you something to push against.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. Receptive, a little dreamy, hard to pin to one shape, and people feel oddly at ease with you without knowing why. Jupiter rules your rising sign, so the Wheel is at home on this Ascendant too. The card's own planet is at your front door, and you read as someone fortune drifts toward. Openings arrive through warmth and a sort of luck people can feel around you, and first impressions go well because you meet people wherever they are.

Meeting people wherever they are can also mean losing your outline. Sagittarius squares your Ascendant, which you'll notice at the start of things, when a soft, adaptable entrance leaves you agreeing to more than you meant or turning into whatever the other person needs you to be. The Nine of Cups decan sits in the middle of Pisces, Jupiter's slice, so a lucky, contented first impression really is available, as long as you're solid enough to be met.

In a new job it's the role that finds you through a sympathetic word, and the boundaries you forget to set. In a new friendship you're instantly easy to be around and slow to say what you need. In dating you can mirror someone so well they never quite meet you. With someone new, hold one clear line about who you are and let them meet that.
rising.reversed:
The front blurs for a Pisces Ascendant. Reversed, Jupiter at home softens it until it has no edges, so people can't tell what you want or where you stand, and a good opening drifts past because you never quite claimed it. Or you shape yourself so completely to each new person that none of them meets you.

A new colleague finds you agreeable and unreadable. Someone who likes you can't work out whether you're interested. At work it can mean agreeing to a deadline you already know you'll miss. That contented middle decan of yours can tip into wishful pleasing, telling people whatever keeps the moment nice. When you next meet someone, say one plain, specific thing you want, and let yourself be met as someone with edges.

1.upright:
A card of luck in the house of the body and the first impression usually means people are treating you differently, and it can take a while to notice why. The first house is how you walk into a room, how you start things, the face and the body other people meet before they know anything else about you. It's angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever lands here gets seen. The Wheel puts Jupiter at your front door, and Jupiter makes things bigger. You may be coming across as bolder and luckier than you feel.

Aries is the sign that naturally belongs to this house, with Mars as its ruler, so a change here has some push behind it. Mercury has its joy in the first house, which makes it a good place for quick, curious beginnings. Jupiter doesn't do quick. It does big, and the tension is between a doorway built for a sharp start and a card that wants to widen everything, including you. Some people find that exciting. Others find it a bit unsettling, as if they've been handed a larger coat and aren't sure it's theirs yet.

The body can show it, with energy that comes in waves and an appetite that grows along with the confidence. So can the way you dress, a haircut, a change of style that other people comment on before you've noticed it yourself. With new people, introductions may come easily, and invitations you wouldn't have had a year ago. Say yes to the ones that fit the person you're turning into.
1.reversed:
Jupiter reversed in the first house tends to get your size wrong. It can blow the self-image up past what the rest of you can carry, the confidence that promises more than you can deliver, the entrance that's a touch too loud. Or it goes the other way, and you keep presenting an old version of yourself that the rest of your life has moved on from, because changing how you come across feels like losing something.

Either way people respond oddly and you can't work out why. The introduction lands flat, and the pitch that used to work doesn't. In the body it can be running on willpower when your energy's asking for a dip, or an appetite that's got ahead of how active you are. Look honestly at a recent photo of yourself and ask whether it matches who you're trying to be. Then change one visible thing so that it does.

2.upright:
This is the house of actual money. Your pay, your savings, what you own, and the harder-to-measure thing underneath it all, what you think you're worth. It's succedent, the part of the chart that gathers and holds, and the sign that goes with it is Taurus, ruled by Venus. The Wheel landing here usually means your finances are on the move, and with Jupiter as the card's planet the movement tends to be upward. A raise, a new client, a sum you weren't expecting. Just as often it's quieter, a growing sense that you've been charging too little.
