Taurus likes value that lasts, so the money this brings tends to come through something real, work that's good, a thing you make or own that turns out to be worth more than you'd assumed. Luck here rarely looks like a lottery ticket. The tension is between a house that wants to hold on and a card that's all about movement. You'll probably want to bank the good news and stop there. Money in the second house under this card grows by being used, spent well, invested, put to work, and sitting on it tends to keep it small.

At work it may be a chance to earn that comes sideways, through a friend or a coincidence, that you nearly dismiss as too easy. With your own pricing it's the number you've been meaning to raise for a year. Around the house, something sitting in a cupboard might be worth selling or finally using. Put your rate up for the next new piece of work, and see who says yes.
2.reversed:
In the house of money, a reversed Wheel can go a couple of ways, and you'll probably know which one is yours. The first is waiting for luck to fix what steady work would fix better. The bet, the scheme, the side hustle that's about to take off, the spending that runs ahead of the income because a big payment is surely coming. Jupiter overdoes things, and upside down in the second house it overdoes hope.

The second is the reverse, a tight grip, clutching savings against a disaster that isn't coming and saying no to anything that costs. Both tend to come with a shaky sense of your own worth, pricing yourself low and calling it realism, or high on the strength of one good run. Open the banking app, write down what came in and what went out over the last three months, and base the next decision on that page.

3.upright:
The third house is the ordinary talk of a life. Texts, emails, the chat over the fence, a sibling on the phone, the drive to the shops, the thing you're learning on the side. It's cadent, the part of the chart that processes and adjusts. The natural sign is Gemini, ruled by Mercury, and this is one of the places the Wheel is uncomfortable. Jupiter is in detriment in Gemini. It thinks in big pictures, and the third house deals in the exact word, the small errand, the particular fact.

So the friction is easy to name. A lucky change in how you speak and learn wants to go wide, and the house keeps asking for precision. You'll likely find yourself with more to say and a bigger audience for it, a course that opens up, a conversation that leads somewhere, people who want to know what you think. The risk is talking bigger than the facts support. The Moon has its joy in this house, and that helps, because it gives you a feel for the mood under a conversation and stops the big talk going over people's heads.

With a brother or sister, or a neighbour, it can be a shift in how you get on, something coming round that seemed stuck. With learning it's a subject that suddenly opens up and gets serious. Your own writing or speaking might reach further than usual. Keep one foot on the facts, and check the numbers before you send the big email.
3.reversed:
Upside down in the third house, the Wheel talks things up. Jupiter is already awkward in Gemini's house, and reversed it inflates the words. Promises made in conversation that nobody follows up. A story that gets a bit better each time it's told. The lucky outcome described so confidently that everyone, including you, starts treating it as real. There's a lot of noise and not much signal.

With a sibling it's the overstated version of events that puts a strain on things. With study it's the course you've talked about for a year and not started, or started and not finished. Short trips go wrong in small ways, the missed train, the wrong address. The Moon rejoices in this house, and it's asking you to be honest about the mood underneath the chatter. Say the plainer, smaller thing, and check one fact before you repeat it.

4.upright:
Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, and Cancer is the natural sign of the fourth house, so this is one of the houses where the Wheel is most welcome. The fourth is home. The actual place you live, the family you came from and the one you've made, and the private ground you stand on when nobody's looking. It's angular, a corner of the chart where things change for real, and its natural ruler is the Moon. So the luck here moves through belonging and care and the people at your table.

The tension is gentle, but it's there. Even a good change at home can feel like the floor shifting, because this is the house you go to so you don't have to deal with change. Jupiter wants to make the house bigger. More room, more people, more welcome. Part of you may brace against that, the part that liked things small and known. I'd let it grow.

With the home itself it might be a move, a spare room, a garden, a lease that finally comes through. With family it can be an arrival, a reconciliation, or a parent who turns out kinder than you'd expected. Inside, it can feel like belonging somewhere properly for the first time in a while. Set a place for the extra person at the table, and move the furniture so there's room for them.
4.reversed:
Jupiter is exalted in this house's sign even with the card upside down, so the good fortune is still on offer at home. The reversal is in how you meet it. You may be holding the household to the way it was in an easier year and calling that loyalty, when it's closer to fear of the ground moving. The corner of the chart that should be shifting things is stuck.

With family it's the pattern everyone has outgrown and nobody will name, Sunday lunch run exactly the way it was when the kids were small. With the house itself it's staying put past the point it suits you, or the renovation you can't start because the rooms have memories in them. The Moon rules the fourth, and it's asking you to trust that belonging survives change. Change one thing at home that everyone's quietly wanted changed, and see who's relieved.

5.upright:
Luck in the house of fun is about as good as a card gets. The fifth house is the part of life you do for the pleasure of it, romance, children, the thing you make because you want to, the Saturday spent on a hobby nobody's paying you for. It's succedent, where the things you love get built up over time. Leo is its sign in the natural zodiac, the Sun its ruler, and Venus has its joy here. Put Jupiter on top of all that and you get generous timing, a romance that starts at the right moment, a creative piece that finds its people, a child who suddenly takes off at something.

The one catch is Leo's fixed streak. When something lovely happens in the fifth house you want to keep it exactly as it is, the first months of a relationship, the buzz of a project that went well, and the Wheel keeps going round whether you like it or not. You can spoil a good thing by trying to repeat it. The better move is to let it turn into whatever it's becoming, and enjoy each version.

In love, a lucky shift might renew something you have or bring someone new along. With creative work, it's a good time to put the thing out where people can see it. With children, yours or any you're close to, there's likely a warm, expansive phase worth being around for. Make something for the fun of it and show it to one person.
5.reversed:
The fifth house reversed tends to overdo the fun or try to pin it down. Jupiter chases the high. The romance gets talked up into something it isn't, the creative buzz gets spent planning the next triumph, one night out becomes three. Or you freeze a good moment so hard it can't grow into the next one, and the delight goes flat under the weight of being protected.

In love it looks like clinging to how the spark felt at the start. With creative work it's repeating the thing that once landed instead of risking something new. With children it can be needing them to keep succeeding the way they did last year. Venus is happiest in the fifth when pleasure is held lightly. Do something enjoyable you've never done before, and don't take a photo of it.

6.upright:
The ordinary week lives in the sixth house. The job you actually do between nine and five, the lunches, the dishes, the gym bag by the door, and the body's upkeep, sleep, food, the walk you keep meaning to take. It's cadent, a house of adjusting and serving, and it lines up with Virgo, ruled by Mercury. Virgo is where Jupiter sits in detriment, so the Wheel works against the grain here. Jupiter likes to go big. The sixth house works through small repeated things, and the two don't naturally agree.

What this usually feels like is an urge to overhaul everything. A lucky change is coming to your routine or your work, and Jupiter wants to meet it with a whole new regime, up at five, new diet, new system, all starting Monday. Most people who try that in the sixth house are back to the old routine within a fortnight. Mars has its joy in this house, which gives the daily grind some drive, and that drive does best aimed at one thing at a time.

At work it might be an improvement in the day-to-day, better hours, a new tool, a colleague who takes something off your plate. With your body it's energy moving into a better phase, which you keep by building on it slowly. Your routine as a whole has room for a better rhythm. Choose one habit, make it small enough to keep on a bad day, and keep it.
6.reversed:
Upside down in the sixth, the Wheel swings between too much and nothing. Jupiter is uncomfortable in Virgo's house, and reversed it overreaches in the daily round. The health kick that burns out in ten days. The treat that becomes a habit. A to-do list so long it guarantees failure. Then the collapse, the routine dropped entirely, the gym bag unpacked and put away.

The body usually tells you first, with tiredness that sleep doesn't fix, or restlessness that has nowhere to go. At work it's a daily load bigger than one person can carry, or tasks left until they pile up and jam. Mars rejoices in this house and likes energy that gets used. Keep the one small habit that actually holds, and let go of the three that only make you feel guilty.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person across the table. A partner, a spouse, a business partner, the one client who matters, anyone you've got an agreement with, written down or not. It's angular, a corner of the chart where things get decided, and Libra is its natural sign, with Venus as ruler. With the Wheel here, a one-to-one relationship is probably at a turning point. Jupiter tends to make that a good turn, a relationship renewed, the right person arriving when you'd stopped looking, a partnership opening onto new ground.

The tension is control. Angular houses want to act, and in a relationship acting often means steering the other person, deciding for both of you how the next phase is going to go. The Wheel doesn't work like that. It changes the situation you're both in, and each of you has to move with it. Venus rules this house and likes things fair, and the fair version is that neither of you gets to set the new terms alone.

With a partner it could be a move, a commitment, a new chapter you both walked into without planning it. In business it's a contract or a deal where timing is doing half the work. If you're single, it might be the introduction through a friend at the dinner you nearly skipped. Have the conversation about what the two of you want next, and let them speak first.
7.reversed:
Someone in the partnership is holding onto a chapter that's already closing. It might be you, and it might be them. One of you is still living in the relationship as it was two years ago, and the other has moved on. With the Wheel reversed in the seventh house, Jupiter can also leave a partnership to luck, trusting it to sort itself out without anybody doing the work.

At home it's the standoff nobody names, each of you waiting for the other to change back. In business it's a partner or client you've stopped really working with, still there on paper and coasting. Venus rules the seventh and asks for some grace toward what the bond is turning into. Ask the other person one straight question about where they think the two of you are, and listen to the whole answer.

8.upright:
Shared money, intimacy and endings all live in the eighth house, and none of them are things you control on your own. Joint accounts, a mortgage, debt, tax, an inheritance, your partner's money and how it mixes with yours. Sex, and the kind of trust sex asks for. The things that have to finish before something else can start. It's succedent, a house of holding, and it's Scorpio's house in the natural chart, ruled by Mars and in modern charts Pluto.

A Jupiter card here tends to mean growth on the far side of a loss. Something shared is changing, and the change is likely to leave you better off. The tension is Scorpio's grip. The eighth house holds on hard, to a person, to money, to the way things were, and the Wheel keeps asking you to let the finished thing finish. It can be a debt paid off after years, a joint account closed, a relationship that ends properly and without a war. None of those feel lucky while they're happening, and most people only see the luck in them a year or two later.

With shared money it might be an inheritance, a settlement, or a joint investment that finally pays. In intimacy it can be a deepening that asks you to let an older version of the relationship go. And an ending you've been dreading may turn out to be where something starts. Pay off or close one shared thing that's been hanging over you.
8.reversed:
Upside down in the eighth, the Wheel usually shows someone gripping what's ending. A joint account nobody will close, a debt nobody will talk about, a relationship kept going in a shape that's already gone, because the empty space afterwards is frightening. Jupiter reversed can also overreach with shared money, a gamble with the joint savings, too much faith that luck will carry what needs actual tending.

With shared resources it looks like holding on to money or power that isn't really yours to hold anymore. In intimacy it can mean staying physically close while being somewhere else emotionally, or the other way round. Mars rules this house, and here that means it takes some nerve to let go. Find the shared paperwork you've been avoiding, the will, the loan, the joint card, and deal with one piece of it.

9.upright:
Jupiter is the natural ruler of the ninth house, so the Wheel is on home turf here, and it shows. This is the house of the long view. Travel, especially far away. Study, the degree or the course or the book that changes how you think. Belief, whatever you'd call your philosophy. It's cadent, and its natural sign is Sagittarius, Jupiter's own. The Sun has its joy here too, which gives the whole house a sense of purpose. A turn of luck in the ninth tends to make your world bigger, and it usually arrives feeling natural, as if it was always going to happen.

Because the card is so at home, the risk here is excess. A lucky break in the ninth can inflate into a kind of faith that doesn't bother checking anything, a plan for a year abroad with no budget, a belief so sure of itself it stops asking questions. Most of the trouble in this pairing comes from skipping the boring checks.

With study it might be the course you finally get into, or a teacher who changes things for you. With travel, an invitation, a job that comes with distance, a trip that turns into something bigger. With belief, a shift in how you understand your own life that makes the hard parts make more sense. Book the thing, sign up for the course, and do the dull paperwork for it straight away.
9.reversed:
In its own house, Jupiter's optimism runs strong even reversed, and the trouble is that it floats off. The faith that only trusts life while things are going well. The grand plan for somewhere else that's really a way to avoid the life in front of you. The course or the retreat or the move overseas that's being sold to you, or that you're selling to yourself, as the answer to everything.

With study it's the big idea that never gets grounded in actual work, the thesis that stays a conversation. With travel it's escape dressed up as a quest. With belief it's a certainty that won't sit through a bad patch. The Sun rejoices in this house and wants a purpose that can survive a low stretch. Ask yourself the hard question you've been skating over, and write the answer down.

10.upright:
Your public life sits in the tenth house. The job title, the reputation, what people say about you when they're asked what you do. It's the most exposed corner of the chart, angular and on show, and it corresponds to Capricorn, ruled by Saturn. That's where this card gets complicated. Jupiter is in fall in Capricorn, uncomfortable and not quite listened to, so the Wheel's easy luck has to find an indirect way up to the top. Saturn wants recognition earned slowly. Jupiter hands out breaks.

What that feels like, usually, is suspicion of your own good fortune. A promotion comes through a connection, or a bit of timing, or someone leaving, and part of you feels it doesn't count because you didn't grind for it. I've seen people turn down perfectly good openings in the tenth for exactly that reason. Jupiter in this house does its job the long way round, and part of the long way is you accepting a turn you didn't manufacture.

In your career it might be an opening a level above where you are, arriving sideways. With your reputation, your name may start getting mentioned in rooms you're not in. Higher up, the people at the top are moving too, and a vacancy can open that nobody expected. When it comes, take the meeting and say plainly what you'd do with the role.
10.reversed:
In the house of career, the reversed Wheel tends to catch you forcing your standing back to where it was. The role's in a down phase, the company's changing, the field has moved on, and you're pushing hard to make things look the way they used to. Jupiter in fall, upside down, can also gamble the reputation on a break, betting on the big pitch when the ordinary work hasn't been done.

It shows as clinging to a job title that's lost its meaning, or overselling a name the results don't back up yet. It shows at performance reviews, and in the quiet worry about who's being promoted past you. Saturn rules the tenth and respects patient, real work. Stop propping up how things looked, and put the energy into one piece of work that will still be good in a year.

11.upright:
Jupiter has its joy in the eleventh house. Of the twelve, it's the one where the planet does its best work, so the Wheel here is about as lucky as this card gets. The eleventh is friends, groups, networks, the people you know through the people you know, and the hopes you have for the next few years. It's succedent, a house of building things up. The natural sign is Aquarius, ruled by Saturn and in modern charts Uranus. The luck in this house comes through other people, almost always.

There isn't much struggle in this pairing, and I wouldn't go looking for any. The small risk is overreach, a hope inflated past what anyone's actually offering, a network that promises more than it delivers. Aquarius is fixed air, and that fixed streak can keep you loyal to a group or a plan after its time has passed. Mostly, though, this is good fortune arriving through belonging, the friend who knows someone, the committee you nearly didn't join, the group chat that turns into a business.

With friends, one of them is likely to open a door for you, and it's worth letting them. With your hopes, something you'd filed under someday gets closer. With a club or an organisation, the shared momentum can carry you further than your own effort would. Tell three people what you're hoping for, specifically, and see who says they know someone.
11.reversed:
Jupiter still does good work in the eleventh even reversed, so the luck isn't far off. What usually goes wrong is either the hope or the circle. A hope gets inflated past what's real, the plan the whole group talks about every time you meet and nobody's done a thing toward. Or the circle feels stuck, and you keep turning up to a group, a friendship, an old crowd, out of habit after it's stopped fitting.

With friends it's the catch-up you dread and keep booking. With your hopes it's a dream you've told everyone about and privately stopped believing in. Saturn rules this house and likes a hope with some work attached. Let one group or friendship change shape without a fight, and pick one hope to put an actual hour into.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is what goes on out of sight. Sleep and dreams, time alone, the parts of you that you don't show anyone, the things working away in the background before they surface. It's cadent, a house of letting go, and it belongs to Pisces in the natural zodiac, a sign Jupiter traditionally rules. So the card's planet is on home turf here, and the Wheel suggests something good is already moving before there's any sign of it. It's the quietest kind of luck.

Saturn has its joy in the twelfth, which adds some structure to what could be a very vague house. The tension is patience. The twelfth asks you to trust a change you can't point to yet, and to trust it while resting, which is hard when you'd prefer to be doing something. If you drag it into the open too early, or keep checking on it, it tends to stall. Leave it be for a while.

With sleep, you may find you need more of it, and dreams get vivid and oddly useful. Time alone, a weekend by yourself or a quiet stretch at home, can do more for you than any amount of socialising. An old worry or habit that's been running in the background may loosen without you forcing it. Give yourself one properly empty day, no plans and no screens, and see what comes up.
12.reversed:
Something is working against you out of sight when the Wheel reverses in the twelfth. Jupiter is still at home here, so the good turn is real, but an old fear or a habit you haven't looked at is dragging on it. The resentment you've never said out loud. The thing you do every night so you don't have to think. It steers your days without asking permission.

It shows in sleep, restless or too heavy, and in a tiredness nobody can quite explain. It shows in the ways you escape, the scrolling, the extra drink, the long hours in bed on a Sunday. Saturn, which rejoices in the twelfth, likes things named and given a shape. Write down the one thing you most avoid thinking about, and tell one person you trust that you did.
